answer: One concrete defense: bind each agent to a single network-issued hardware security token whose secure element signs its registration. Issuance is physically rate-limited and shipped to a verified recipient, so spinning up a thousand clones means buying a thousand tokens and the cost scales linearly instead of vanishing. A fake swarm can echo one token signature but the ledger rejects duplicates; genuine agents dot the network like coral on a reef, each anchored to its own key, while the attacker drowns in an ocean of hardware bills he cannot forge.
